subject: P99 + throughput jitter — coordinated mitigation & customer note
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: [Action needed] P99 latency + throughput jitter on hosted-us-west-2

Logan / team,

We started seeing a sustained P99 jump in hosted-us-west-2 starting ~07:58 PDT. Key observations so far:
- P99 token latency for text-generation endpoint up from ~220ms to ~1.7s (rolling 5m).
- Aggregate throughput (tokens/sec) for the 2x family down ~28% vs baseline.
- Error rate is stable (<=0.1%), so this looks like tail/queuing, not a model failure.
- Autoscaler did two additional capacity adds between 08:02-08:06 but p99 did not improve.

Immediate asks:
1) Can product/ops confirm which model variants are safe to route to as a fallback (quality impact acceptable vs default)?
2) SRE: please advise whether enabling prefix/KV cache TTL or temporary routing to quantized variants is safe for QuickCommerce traffic.
3) Sales/AM (Logan): we should prepare a short customer note (1-2 lines) explaining impact and expected mitigation timeline; draft suggested below.

I've attached a screenshot and the initial 5m metrics export. Marcus/Hannah, booking a 30-min bridge if we need to escalate.

Attachments: incident_screenshot.png, initial-metrics.csv

Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@quickcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Action needed] P99 latency + throughput jitter on hosted-us-west-2

Thanks Marissa — flagged and appreciate the triage.

Elena (cc'd): we see a P99 latency spike affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2; engineering is investigating. I wanted to loop you in proactively and will share an explicit customer-facing line once we have the short mitigation plan.

Marissa / Marcus: two quick product questions for routing guidance so I can set expectations:
- Which fallback model variant do you recommend that minimizes end-user quality impact (and what's the rough delta in output fidelity)?
- If we route 10-20% traffic to that fallback, do we expect the P99 to drop into acceptable SLO range (~<500ms)?

If we can get those answers in the next 15–20 minutes I will send a short note to QuickCommerce ops. Otherwise, I will indicate we are investigating and will follow up with details.

Also propose a 08:30 bridge (15m) to align on a fast mitigation.

—Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Action needed] P99 latency + throughput jitter on hosted-us-west-2

Quick update from runtime side:
- Short term (now): enable routing rule that shifts 10% traffic to quantized-v2 (lower mem/KV pressure) and bump KV-cache TTL to 60s for repeated prefixes. Command we can apply: `rb route apply --env hosted-us-west-2 --rule fallback-quantized-v2 --pct 10`
- Expected effect: P99 should drop ~30-45% on affected workload (based on sim from last week), throughput should recover as queuing reduces. Quality impact: minimal for short prompts; longer chained prompts may show slight token-level divergence.
- Rollback: `rb route remove --rule fallback-quantized-v2` — immediate revert.

I'm standing by to execute once we have sign-off. I'll also watch the KV eviction counters and scheduler queue length and report back.

Marcus
Staff SW Eng, Serving Runtime
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:48:00-07:00
Subject: QuickCommerce — brief status note (draft)

Hi Elena,

Draft for your review — short, transparent, and sets a near-term expectation. Please let me know if you'd like any edits before I send from operations: 

--- DRAFT START ---
Hi QuickCommerce ops team,

We are investigating an elevated latency event impacting a portion of traffic in the us-west-2 region. Our SREs are applying a temporary routing adjustment that should restore expected response times within ~20–30 minutes. We do not currently see increased error rates or data integrity issues.

We will follow up with a brief post-incident note outlining cause and any customer-facing mitigations. If you see any customer-impacting errors or degraded outputs, please reply to this thread and we will prioritize.

Thanks for your patience,
Logan (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
--- DRAFT END ---

Attachments: qc_customer_note_v1.txt

Marissa / Marcus / Hannah — please confirm if I should include the quantized fallback line (we should avoid technical jargon for the customer unless you advise otherwise).

—Logan
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@quickcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickCommerce — brief status note (draft)

Looks good. Confirming the bridge at 08:30 PDT (I'll open the incident page and own the timeline updates). Action items:
- Marcus: apply 10% route to quantized-v2 and increase KV TTL to 60s (now).
- Marissa: watch P99 and scheduler queue; call back when P99 <= 500ms or if error rate rises.
- Logan: send customer note now with language as drafted (no vendor-facing technical detail).

I'll post an update on https://status.redwood.com/incident/INC-3489 and we can reconvene at 09:00 to decide on further action or rollback.

Hannah
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
